cards.q: What replaces coding puzzles in the internal A3 assessment?
cards.a: A committee defense of your real project work, scored against the competency matrix.

cards.q: Name the 5-part structure for presenting your project.
cards.a: Problem, constraints, 2–3 design options with tradeoffs, chosen design rationale, measured outcome.
Your manager (sponsorship) plus a readiness review.

cards.q: What is the single biggest defense mistake?
cards.a: Describing team achievements with "we" and never owning a decision with "I".

cards.q: What is the repeating framework across all 11 GenAI design chapters?
cards.a: Clarify requirements → frame as ML task → data preparation → model development → evaluation → overall system design, with deployment + monitoring on top.

cards.q: How do you pick the generative model family?
cards.a: Requirements arithmetic: one-pass latency → GAN/VAE, ceiling quality → diffusion, resolution at scale → autoregressive tokens, video economics → latent diffusion.

cards.q: Why retrieval (RAG) before finetuning for knowledge injection?
cards.a: Finetuning can't cite sources and needs constant retraining; RAG balances cost, scalability, freshness — RAFT finetuning only after retrieval is fixed.

cards.q: What must accompany offline metrics in a GenAI evaluation answer?
cards.a: Online business metrics — CTR, adoption, cost per user per month — because users re-roll failed generations and burn GPU money; name both unprompted.

Columnar file format with per-column encoding and nested-type support.

Redistributing data across partitions between stages; the dominant Spark cost.
Uneven key distribution making one partition dominate stage time.
Durable snapshot of Flink state enabling exactly-once recovery.
Merging small files into fewer large ones to restore read performance.
Multi-column clustering of lakehouse files to prune scans on any column.
Broadcast vs sort-merge vs shuffle-hash — picked by size + skew stats.
Versioned repository of point-in-time-correct features for training and serving.

exactly-once is engineered from idempotent writes.
lakehouse layers are stored in open columnar formats.
retrieval quality depends on embedding similarity.

Bring: problem → constraints → 2–3 design options → tradeoff rationale → measured outcome.

16: The skeleton is the transferable asset: clarify requirements → frame as ML task → data → model → eval → system design + deployment/monitoring — one rehearsal covers any prompt.
Model choice is requirements arithmetic, not fashion: one-pass latency → GAN/VAE, ceiling quality → diffusion, resolution at scale → AR, video economics → latent diffusion.
Exhaust retrieval + prompts before finetuning: finetuning can't cite sources and needs constant retraining; RAFT only when retrieval is fixed and answers are still bad.
RAG pipeline: parse → chunk (500 chars, 200 overlap) → embed → ANN-index; size it explicitly — 5M pages → 40M chunks, +20%/yr.
Retrieval quality is the ceiling: a better LLM cannot fix bad chunks.
Pair offline metrics (BLEU, CIDEr, CLIPScore, FID/FVD, DINO) with online business metrics (CTR, adoption, cost per user) — naming both unprompted is the scoring behavior.
Deployment is a named stage: safety chain, serving, monitoring, retraining loops — users re-rolling seeds quietly multiplies GPU spend.
